rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd reports that after the Messenger summoned his close relatives to God, Abū Lahab said he would ransom himself with wealth and children if his nephew’s claim were true; the verse was then revealed.
rows.anchor: قال ابن مسعود : لما دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أقرباءه إلى الله عز وجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Baghawī glosses the clause as asking what benefit Abū Lahab's wealth could bring him.
rows.anchor: { ما أغنى عنه ماله } أي ما يغني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative gloss asks what thing his wealth could avail him.
rows.anchor: وقيل : أي شيء يغني عنه ماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wealth Abū Lahab gathered could not ward off God's punishment from him.
rows.anchor: أي : ما يدفع عنه عذاب الله ما جمع من المال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative gloss takes what Abū Lahab earned to mean his child, since a person's child is considered part of his earnings, as the hadith indicates.
rows.anchor: قيل : يعني ولده ؛ لأن ولد الإنسان من كسبه ، كما جاء في الحديث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites an unattributed hadith saying that the best food a person eats comes from his earnings and that his child is from his earnings.
rows.anchor: أطيب ما يأكل أحدكم من كسبه ، وإن ولده من كسبه
